summaries.Good news: Today's heartwarming stories celebrate resilience and restoration—from a deaf BSL interpreter bringing live music to deaf audiences through innovative interpretation, to ospreys making a remarkable comeback in Britain after a century of extinction. Real human creativity and nature's recovery are both on full display.
summaries.Ideas: The day's ideas explore systemic challenges and human consequences: how AI is reshaping workplace culture and trust, the toll of surveillance technology on privacy, and the urgent need for design-centered change management in organizations facing digital transformation.
summaries.Technology: Innovation spans autonomous systems and efficiency records: from AI-equipped sonar systems revolutionizing naval operations to Nissan's record-breaking fuel economy hybrid, plus clever product engineering from robot cameras to portable car wash devices addressing everyday frustrations.
summaries.Design: Today's design work showcases architecture's power to transform: landmark civic projects (German House redesign in NYC, MIT's warehouse conversion), intimate human-centered spaces (a wellness studio designed as a journey inward), and thoughtful retail environments that respect local culture without cliché.

items.title: There’s a Fatty Liver Epidemic. AI Could Help Get Ahead of It
items.snippet: Over a billion people worldwide have livers with excess fat, which can lead to a host of medical problems. Researchers think AI tools can spot the condition—and help stop it—early enough to save lives.
items.line: AI tools trained to detect fatty liver disease early could prevent a billion-person epidemic before it becomes symptomatic, showing how machine learning serves preventive medicine at scale.

items.line: A designer enzyme that reverses sugar damage in aging tissue—making 75-year-old cells biochemically resemble 30-year-old ones—represents a breakthrough in understanding and potentially reversing cellular aging.
